summary: This document defines an RTCP Extended Report block for reporting decodability statistics of MPEG2 Transport Streams carried over RTP, which is widely used in IPTV. It helps monitor stream quality.

eli5.summary: When you watch TV sent over the Internet, the receiver can check whether it understood the pieces. This RFC adds a report that says how well the picture information was readable.

subtitle: A new RTCP report block that counts PSI errors in MPEG2 transport streams, so IPTV receivers can say how decodable a stream is.

tldr.problem: MPEG2 Transport Streams carried over RTP are widely used in IPTV, but RTCP had no way to report whether the Program Specific Information inside a stream was healthy enough to decode.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an RTCP XR block (block type 32) that carries seven 16-bit counters taken from ETSI TR 101 290 tests: PAT, PAT2, PMT, PMT2, PID, CRC and CAT errors over a range of RTP sequence numbers.
tldr.outcome: Operators and monitoring tools can now collect PSI error counts from receivers alongside other RTCP data. It supplements the PSI-independent metrics of RFC 6990.

today: RFC 7380 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2014, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It supplements the PSI-independent block of RFC 6990.

sections.title: Why Report PSI Decodability
sections.content:
An MPEG2 Transport Stream (TS) is a standard container format for multimedia data, and sending it over RTP is widely deployed in IPTV systems. This RFC defines a new RTCP Extended Report (XR) block that reports decodability statistics related to the Program Specific Information (PSI) carried in the TS.

The metrics come from a set of tests published by ETSI (ETSI TR 101 290), which groups indicators by priority: first priority is necessary for decodability, second priority is recommended for continuous or periodic monitoring, and third priority is for application-dependent monitoring. This block reports occurrence counts for the first and second priority PSI indicators only. Third priority indicators are not supported.
sections.eli5: Think of a TV signal as a book with a table of contents. This RFC gives receivers a way to report how often the table of contents was broken.

sections.title: Where the Block Fits
sections.content:
RTCP reporting is defined in RFC 3550, and RFC 3611 defines the extensible XR report structure. This document adds one more block type to that structure. It also supplements the PSI-Independent Decodability Statistics Metrics Block from RFC 6990, and follows the Performance Metrics Framework (RFC 6390) and the RTP monitoring guidelines (RFC 6792).

The metrics apply to any RTP application that uses the MPEG2 TS format, for example MPEG4 over MPEG2 TS over RTP. They can help measure content stream or TS quality by checking TS header information, and can reveal packetization problems that may affect what users see. They may also help verify that an existing system management tool still works correctly.
sections.eli5: The report rides along with the normal status messages that video senders and receivers already swap. It just adds one more kind of note.

sections.title: The Block Layout
sections.content:
The block is measured at the receiving end of the RTP stream. It has a block type (BT) of 32, a reserved byte, a block length of 6, the SSRC of the source, begin_seq and end_seq, and then seven 16-bit counters followed by 16 reserved bits.

The block length MUST be the constant 6, and a block with any other value MUST be discarded. Reserved bits MUST be set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers. The SSRC, begin_seq and end_seq fields are defined as in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611; every count covers the sequence number interval they delimit.
sections.eli5: The report is a small form with a fixed number of boxes. There is a box for who it is about, the range of packets it covers, and seven counting boxes.

sections.title: The Seven Counters
sections.content:
Five counters cover basic monitoring needed to decode the stream: PAT_error_count, PAT_error_2_count, PMT_error_count, PMT_error_2_count and PID_error_count. Two cover continuous monitoring: CRC_error_count and CAT_error_count.

  • A PAT error occurs when a packet with PID 0x0000 does not occur at least every 0.5 seconds, does not contain table_id 0x00, or has a non-zero scrambling control field. The PAT lists every program in the stream, so if it is missing no programs can be decoded.
  • A PMT error occurs when a packet with table_id 0x02 does not occur at least every 0.5 seconds on the PID referred to in the PAT, or when scrambling control is not 00.
  • A PID error occurs when no data stream is present for a given PID, which may be caused by multiplexing or demultiplexing and then remultiplexing.
  • A CRC error means data corruption in any of the CAT, PAT, PMT, NIT, EIT, BAT, SDT or TOT tables.
  • A CAT error occurs when a packet with PID 0x0001 carries a table_id other than 0x01, or when scrambling is employed and no CAT is present.

The PAT2 and PMT2 counters are replacements and improvements on the PAT and PMT counters, so they are preferred in future implementations. If PAT_error_2_count or PMT_error_2_count is available (not 0xFFFF), receivers MUST ignore the older counter. Any measurement that is unavailable MUST be reported as 0xFFFF.
sections.eli5: Each counter is a tally of one kind of mistake, like a missing table of contents or a corrupted page. If a counter cannot be measured, the report says so with a special all-ones number.

sections.title: Signaling with SDP
sections.content:
RFC 3611 defines how the Session Description Protocol signals use of XR blocks, though XR blocks MAY be used without prior signaling. This RFC adds a new value for the rtcp-xr attribute: xr-format =/ xr-tpd-block, where xr-tpd-block = "ts-psi-decodability".

Offer/Answer usage follows the unilateral parameter rules in Section 5.2 of RFC 3611, and usage outside Offer/Answer follows Section 5.3 of RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: Before the report is sent, two sides can tell each other they understand it by using a short agreed name, ts-psi-decodability.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC assigns block type value 32, named "MPEG2 Transport Stream PSI Decodability Statistics Metrics Block", in the RTCP XR Block Type subregistry. It also registers the parameter ts-psi-decodability in the RTCP XR SDP Parameters subregistry. The contact for both registrations is the RAI Area Directors.
sections.eli5: The number 32 and the name were written into the official list so nobody else uses them for something different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The block introduces no new security considerations beyond those described in RFC 3611 and RFC 6990.
sections.eli5: This new report does not add any new safety worries beyond what the older reports already have.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero by senders, ignored by receivers.

fields.name: begin_seq
fields.desc: Start of the sequence number interval.

fields.name: end_seq
fields.desc: End of the sequence number interval.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero by senders, ignored by receivers.
